ausparl: Query the Australian Parliamentary Hansard Database

Source: R/ausparl-package.R
ausparl-package.Rd

ausparl gives basic, reproducible query access to the Australian Parliamentary Hansard: the record of debates in the House of Representatives and the Senate since 1901, held in a pre-built DuckDB database and linked to members, parties, ministries and electorates from the Parliamentary Handbook. Queries run inside the database and only their results come back into R; the database is opened read-only and never loaded into memory.

Start with vignette("database"), a guide to the tables, identifiers and conventions of the database.

Getting the database

The full database (about 9.5 GB) is not installed with the package. db_download() fetches the version this release pins from Zenodo and checks it, and db_connect() then opens it with no arguments. A small sample database of eight sitting days is bundled for examples and tests: db_connect(sample = TRUE).

db_connect() chooses the file in this order: an explicit path (or sample = TRUE), then the AUSPARL_DB environment variable, then the copy installed by db_download(), then the full database used earlier in the session, then hansard.duckdb in the working directory or its dataset/ folder. Query functions connect on first use if no connection is open.

Functions by task

  • Connection: db_download(), db_connect(), db_disconnect(), db_info(), db_con(), db_tbl().

  • Speeches and search: get_speeches() (one row per action), get_speech_turns() (consecutive actions by one speaker merged into a turn), search_speeches_by_terms() (full-text search with hit counts), get_sitting_timeline() (a sitting in document order) and get_interjections() (who interrupted whom).

  • Members: find_member() to look up a PHID by name, and member_profile() for everything recorded about one member.

  • Activity summaries: member_activity(), party_activity(), parliament_summary().

  • Context on the day of a turn: add_party(), add_role(), add_government_status(), add_electorate(), add_age(), add_member(), add_debate().

  • Tables: one getter per table: get_sittings(), get_debates(), get_subdebates(), get_actions(), get_members(), get_parliaments(), get_parties(), get_party_service(), get_parl_service(), get_electorates(), get_elections(), get_ministries(), get_ministry_records(), get_shadow_ministry_records(), get_committee_members(), get_presiding_officers(), get_occupations(), get_qualifications(), get_schools() and get_provenance(). Any other table or view is available with db_tbl().

  • Filter helpers: in_range() and matches_pattern(), accepted by most filter arguments.

  • Outputs: as_corpus() hands text to quanteda, and result_provenance() lists the source files behind a result.

Common arguments

Most query functions share three arguments:

  • collect: TRUE (the default) returns a tibble; FALSE returns a lazy dplyr table that you can keep filtering, joining and summarising inside DuckDB before calling dplyr::collect().

  • limit: the maximum number of rows to return, or NULL for no limit.

  • columns: the columns to return, or NULL for all.

Chamber arguments take "house" and/or "senate", in any case. Date bounds (from, to) take a year (covering the whole year), a Date or a "YYYY-MM-DD" string, and are inclusive.

Package options

  • ausparl.memory_limit: the cap on DuckDB's memory use, a size such as "1.5GB". Default "3GB". Takes effect at the next db_connect().

  • ausparl.max_rows: the most rows a result without speech text may collect into R; a larger result is an error that suggests collect = FALSE. Default 2,000,000. Inf switches the check off.

  • ausparl.max_rows_text: the same ceiling for results that include the speech text (content). Default 800,000.

  • ausparl.auto_install_fts: whether db_connect() may install DuckDB's full-text-search extension when it is missing (a one-off download). Default TRUE.

Environment variables

  • AUSPARL_DB: path to a hansard.duckdb file, used by db_connect() when no path is given. Set it in ~/.Renviron to use the same copy in every session.

  • R_USER_DATA_DIR: moves the user data directory in which db_download() installs the database by default (see tools::R_user_dir()).

Versions and citation

Each ausparl release pins exactly one database version, recorded in the package DESCRIPTION (Config/ausparl/data_version) and archived on Zenodo. db_info() reports the version and build time of the database you are connected to; quote them in your methods. To cite the package, run citation("ausparl").
